s: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to which ruler?
x: Errana dedicated his Harivamsam to Prolaya Vema Reddi.

s: Who wrote Bogini Dandakam?
x: Bogini Dandakam is by Bammera Potana, a contemporary of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and Srinatha.

s: Which work of Srinatha is associated with Bhimeswara of Draksharamam?
x: Bhimakhandam, also known as Bhimeswara Puranam, praises Bhimeswara of Draksharamam.

s: Which of the following works was NOT associated with Errana?
x: Errana is associated with Aranya Parva shesham, Harivamsam and Nrusimha Puranam. Palnati Veera Charitra was one of Srinatha's works.

s: To whom did Srinatha dedicate his Sringara Naishadham?
x: Sringara Naishadham, based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita, was dedicated to Mamidi Singana; Haravilasam went to Tippayya Setti.

s: Who wrote Usha Parinayam?
x: Vamana Bhanu Bhattu wrote Usha Parinayam; Bammera Potana wrote Veera Bhadra Vijayam.

s: Who wrote Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam?
x: Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam is by Vamana Bhanu Bhattu; Haravilasam, Srungara Naishadham and Palnati Veera Charitra are Srinatha's.

s: Which of the following descriptions of Errana is correct?
o: He was the first of the Kavitrayam and initiated the Telugu Mahabharata.
He was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata.
He opened the Kavya Yuga through his independent Sanskrit compositions.
He was a court poet of the Vijayanagara emperor who translated the entire Sanskrit Mahabharata.
x: Errana was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata by translating the remaining portion of the Aranya Parva.

s: Which of the following titles was borne by the poet Errana?
x: Errana was called Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Sahitya Chudamani was Vamana Bhatta Bana's. Andhra Suratrana was a royal title (Anavema in the APPSC key, first borne by Kapaya Nayaka), not a poet's.

s: At Vijayanagara, Srinatha defeated which court poet of Devaraya II?
x: Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta of Devaraya II's court and was honoured with Kanakabhishekam.

s: Who is traditionally associated with opening the Kavya Yuga in Telugu literature?
x: Srinatha is described as the poet who opened the Kavya Yuga, whereas Errana completed the Andhra Mahabharata as the last of the Kavitrayam.

s: Which portion of the Telugu Mahabharata did Errana complete?
x: Errana, last of the Kavitrayam, completed the Telugu Mahabharata with the remaining Aranya Parva (Aranya Parva shesham).

s: Who wrote Vema Bhupala Charitra, a prose biography of Pedakomati Vema?
x: Vamana Bhatta Bana, court poet of Pedakomati Vema, wrote Vema Bhupala Charitra.

s: Srinatha held which office at the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddi?
x: Srinatha (Kavi Sarvabhauma) was Vidyadhikari, the minister of education, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, and he composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions. He held no post as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.

s: Who was the last poet of the Kavitrayam?
x: Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam.

s: Which work of Srinatha describes the life of the people of Palnadu?
x: Srinatha's Palnati Veera Charitra describes the life and battle of Palnadu.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Srinatha's writings are cited as evidence of the use of paper in the 15th century.
2. Madanavilasabanam is a work of Srinatha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Srinatha is cited for paper use in the 15th century; Madanavilasabanam is not his work.

s: Who composed the Sanskrit inscriptions of Anavota Reddi?
x: Bala Saraswati, Anavota's court poet, composed his Sanskrit inscriptions.

s: Which title was held by Vamana Bhatta Bana, the court poet of Pedakomati Vema Reddi?
x: Vamana Bhatta Bana bore the titles Sahitya Chudamani and Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara.

s: Who wrote Hamsa Sandesam and Nalabhyudayam?
x: Vamana Bhatta Bana of Pedakomati Vema's court wrote Hamsa Sandesam, Nalabhyudayam and other works.

s: After the fall of Kondavidu in 1424, Srinatha joined the court of which Rajahmundry Reddi ruler?
x: After 1424 Srinatha joined Veerabhadra Reddi of Rajahmundry with Bendapudi Annamatya's help.

s: Which honour did Srinatha receive at Deva Raya II's court after defeating Gauda Dindima Bhatta?
x: For defeating Gauda Dindima Bhatta, Srinatha was honoured with Kanakabhishekam (bath of gold coins).

s: On which Sanskrit work is Srinatha's Sringara Naishadham based?
x: Sringara Naishadham is Srinatha's Telugu rendering of Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita.

s: At whose court did Srinatha serve as Vidyadhikari (education minister)?
x: Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at the Kondaveedu court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and wrote the king's Sanskrit inscriptions. Under Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry he wrote Bhimakhandam and Kasikhandam; at Devaraya II's court he won the title Kavi Sarvabhauma; Sarvajna Singabhupala is linked with Potana's refusal of patronage.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajahmundry — Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya
x: After Kondaveedu fell in 1424, Srinatha went to Rajahmundry under Veerabhadra Reddy through Bendapudi Anantamatya. The other pairs confuse patrons or places.

s: Which statement about Srinatha is correct?
o: He pioneered the Prabandha style, and his age is known as the Kavya Yuga.
He founded the Tallapaka tradition of sankirtana.
He was the composer of the Pancharatna Kritis.
He was the first Telugu woman poet and composed Bhogini Dandakam.
x: Srinatha is regarded as a pioneer of the Prabandha style, and his period is called the Kavya Yuga. The other statements refer to different literary or musical figures.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Srinatha's works and their dedications?
x: Sringara Naishadhamu was dedicated to the minister Mamidi, or Madiki, Singana. Haravilasamu was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, while Sivaratri Mahatmyam was dedicated to Mummadi Santayya.

s: After the fall of Rajahmundry, Srinatha's chatu verses chiefly portrayed which condition?
o: The maritime wealth of Avachi Tippaya Setti
The religious debates at the Vijayanagara court
The prosperity of the Gajapati court
The hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu
x: After Rajahmundry fell in 1448, Srinatha lived in poverty in Palnadu. His chatu verses provide a literary picture of its hardship and coarse food.

s: At whose court did Srinatha receive the title Kavi Sarvabhauma?
x: At Vijayanagara Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta before Devaraya II and won Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

s: In which year was the Palnadu war, the subject of the dvipada ballad Palnati Veera Charitra, fought?
x: Palnati Veera Charitra describes the Palnadu war of 1182.

s: In which year did Kondaveedu fall, after which Srinatha moved to the Rajahmundry court?
x: Kondaveedu fell in 1424 and Srinatha went to Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry; Rajahmundry itself fell in 1448.

s: Which of the following works is NOT by Srinatha?
x: Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam and Palnati Veera Charitra are credited to Srinatha; the APPSC Group 2 Mains 2025 key made Madanavilasa Bhanam the 'not by Srinatha' answer.

s: To whom did Srinatha dedicate Sringara Naishadhamu?
x: Sringara Naishadhamu went to minister Mamidi (Madiki) Singana; Haravilasamu to Avachi Tippaya Setti and Sivaratri Mahatmyam to Mummadi Santayya.

s: Who among the following made the first reference to paper as a writing material in Andhra?
x: Srinatha's writings give the first reference to paper as writing material in Andhra.

s: Whom did Srinatha defeat in a literary debate at the court of Devaraya II?
x: At Devaraya II's court in Vijayanagara, Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta, was given Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

s: Who among the following Telugu poets was honoured with Kanakabhishekam at the court of Devaraya II?
x: After defeating Gauda Dindima Bhatta at Devaraya II's court, Srinatha received Kanakabhishekam and the title Kavi Sarvabhauma.

s: At whose court in Rajahmundry did Srinatha write Bhimakhandamu and Kasikhandamu?
x: After Kondaveedu fell in 1424, Srinatha moved to the Rajahmundry court of Veerabhadra Reddy, where he wrote Bhimakhandamu and Kasikhandamu.

s: Who constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to supply water to the tank dug by Surambika?
o: Somaya, the minister of Anavota Reddi
x: Racha Vema, the son of Surambika, constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to feed water into the tank dug by his mother.

s: Which groups formed the warrior-farmer backbone of Kakatiya–Reddi society?
x: Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas formed the warrior-farmer backbone and supplied most of the soldiers.

s: Surambika Reddy was the queen of which ruler?
x: Surambika was the queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and dug the Santana Sagaram tank. Kumaragiri and Prolaya Vema were other Reddy kings, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.

s: At which places were Devadasis, trained in music, dance and ritual, respected performers during the Reddi period?
x: Devadasis were respected performers at Shiva temples, including the Pancharamas.

s: Who financed the Vasantotsavams celebrated at the Reddi court?
x: The merchant Avachi Tippayya Setti funded the Vasantotsavams; this patronage is recorded in Srinatha's Haravilasam.

s: Who wrote 'Karpura Vasanta Rayalu', a work on Kumaragiri Reddi?
x: C. Narayana Reddy wrote Karpura Vasanta Rayalu on Kumaragiri, the patron of Vasantotsavam.

s:
Match the following:
List-I
a. Lakumadevi
b. Surambika
c. Anitalli
List-II
1. Queen of Pedakomati Vema
2. Court dancer of Kumaragiri Reddi
3. Issued the Kaluvacheru inscription
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Lakumadevi was Kumaragiri's court dancer, Surambika was Pedakomati Vema's queen, and Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription.

s: In which dance form was Lakumadevi, the court dancer of Kumaragiri Reddi, an expert?
x: Lakumadevi danced Bharatanatyam at the court of Kumaragiri Reddi, who was himself an expert in Bharata Natya.

s: Who dug the Santana Sagaram tank?
x: Surambika, queen of Pedakomati Vema, dug the Santana Sagaram tank.

s: What was the Ghatika Yantra used in the Reddi period?
x: The Ghatika Yantra was a water clock for measuring time; its keeper was the Ghatikagara.

s: By which title was Kumaragiri Reddi known?
x: Karpura Vasantaraya was Kumaragiri's title; Veeranna Pothu belonged to Anavota, Andhra Suratrana to Anavema and Bharatamata Patanga to Sivalinga Reddi.

s: The musical instrument 'Jalakaranda' is mentioned in which inscription?
x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the 'Jalakaranda' (PYQ G2 2019). The Manyapuram inscription records Anavota's capital shift, Kaluvacheru was issued by Anitalli in 1423, and Sarpavaram concerns Kataya Vema's family and treaty with Harihara II.

s: Which Reddy ruler was an expert in Bharata Natya?
x: Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in dance and wrote Vasantarajeeyam on it. Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sangeeta Chintamani, Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the kingdom, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.

s: Who wrote Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka?
x: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani and Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka.

s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Bammera Potana?
x: Sahitya Chintamani was written by Pedakomati Vema Reddy; Potana wrote Narayana Satakam, Andhra Bhagavatam and Bhogini Dandakam.

s: Singabhupala II, the author of Sangeeta Sudhakaram, belonged to which political group?
x: Singabhupala II was a Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda, not a Reddi ruler, and he wrote Sangeeta Sudhakaram.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Srinatha wrote Srungara Naishadham. Sangeeta Chintamani is by Pedakomati Vema Reddy, Vasantarajeeyam by Kumaragiri Reddy and Gatha Saptasati was compiled by Hala.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vinnakota Peddana wrote Kavyalankara Chudamani. Padma Puranam is by Madiki Singana, Vishnupuranam by Vennalakanti Suranna and Andhra Sabda Chintamani by Nannaya.

s: Who wrote Srungara Deepika, a commentary on Amaru Shataka?
x: Pedakomati Vema wrote Srungara Deepika on Amaru Shataka, besides Sangeeta Chintamani and Sahitya Chintamani.

s: Who wrote Kavyalankara Chudamani, linked to Rajahmundry as a literary hub?
x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; Sivalila Vilasamu is by Sivaleka Kommana and Kashikhandam by Srinatha.

s: Who wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays?
x: Kumaragiri Rajiyam was written by Kataya Vema Reddi, Kumaragiri's brother-in-law, and only named after Kumaragiri.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sarvajna Chakravarti was Pedakomati Vema's title; Kataka Churakara was Kataya Vema's, Dweepa Vijetha Anavota's and Karpura Vasantaraya Kumaragiri's.

s: The Reddi kingdom was established approximately during which period?
x: The Reddi kingdom flourished approximately from 1325 to 1448 CE. The Kondaveedu line continued from about 1325 to 1424, while the Rajamahendravaram line continued from 1402 to 1448.

s: Which of the following correctly gives the dynastic features of the Reddis?
o: Panta vamsam, Bull emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Sanskrit as royal language
Deseti kula, Garuda emblem, Durga as family deity and Telugu as royal language
Panta vamsam, Lion emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Prakrit as royal language
Yadava kula, Bull emblem, Lakshmi as family deity and Kannada as royal language
x: The Reddis belonged to the Panta vamsam, were also associated with the Deseti kula, used the Bull as their emblem, worshipped Mula Guramma and used Sanskrit as the royal language.

s: How is the Reddi rule, dated from about 1325 to 1448, described?
o: The beginning of the Bahmani golden age
The second golden age of Telugu culture
The final age of Chola imperial expansion
The first golden age of Sanskrit culture in the Deccan
x: Reddi rule, approximately from 1325 to 1448, is called the second golden age of Telugu culture.

s: The Reddi kingdoms emerged as one of the three successor states after 1323 along with which two states?
x: The Reddis were one of three successor political formations after 1323, the other two being the Musunuris and the Recherla Velamas.

s: Prolaya Vema Reddy served in whose court, according to the Anitalli inscription?
x: The Anitalli inscription states that Prolaya Vema Reddy served in the court of Kapaya Nayaka, the Musunuri leader who freed Andhra from the Delhi Sultanate.

s: What was the royal emblem of the Reddi kings?
x: The Reddis of the Panta clan had the Bull as emblem and Mula Guramma as family deity.

s: Prolaya Vema Reddi is credited with building how many forts, including Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota?
x: Prolaya Vema Reddi is credited with building 74 forts, including Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota.

s: Which fort replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital?
x: Kondaveedu replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital and later became a battleground between the Gajapatis and Vijayanagara.

s: Which of the following represents the sequence of capitals of the Reddi kingdoms?
x: The capitals successively shifted from Addanki to Kondaveedu and later to Rajamahendravaram.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its region?
x: Kondavidu is associated with the Guntur region, not East Godavari. Addanki is in Prakasam and Kondapalli in Krishna.

s: The Kondapalli hill fort, credited to Prolaya Vema, lies in which region?
x: Kondapalli is a strategic hilltop fort in Krishna; Addanki is in Prakasam and Kondavidu in Guntur.

s: What is the main gate of the Kondapalli fort called?
x: The main gate of Kondapalli fort is the Dargah Darwaza, named after the tomb of Gulab Shah who died in battle there.

s: Which palace stands inside the Kondapalli fort?
x: The Tanisha Mahal palace stands inside Kondapalli fort, between two hills; the main gate is the Dargah Darwaza.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the early political career of Prolaya Vema Reddi?
o: He served in the court of Prataparudra and expelled Tughluq forces from coastal Andhra around 1325.
He served in the court of Deva Raya I and conquered Kalinga around 1404.
He served in the court of Firoz Shah and captured Rajahmundry around 1396.
He served in the court of Harihara II and expelled Gajapati forces from Kondaveedu around 1450.
x: Prolaya Vema Reddi had served in Prataparudra's court and expelled Tughluq forces from coastal Andhra around 1325, with one account placing the event in 1324.

s: From whom did Anavema Reddi take Nidadavolu, Pithapuram, Simhachalam and Konaseema?
x: Anavema conquered Nidadavolu, Rajahmundry, Pithapuram, Simhachalam and Konaseema from the Kalinga Gajapatis (Kandukur was not among them).

s:
Arrange the following rulers of the Kondaveedu Reddi line in chronological order.
A. Anavema Reddi
B. Prolaya Vema Reddi
C. Pedakomati Vema Reddi
D. Kumaragiri Reddi
x: The order is Prolaya Vema Reddi, Anavema Reddi, Kumaragiri Reddi and Pedakomati Vema Reddi.

s: Which Reddi ruler is described as the most charitable among the Reddi kings?
x: Anavema Reddi is noted as the most charitable Reddi king.

s: In which year did Pedakomati Vema oust Kumaragiri Reddi?
x: Pedakomati Vema ousted Kumaragiri in 1402, after which Kumaragiri fled to Rajahmundry.

s: Who was the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi associated with the capture of Motupalli?
x: Mallareddi, the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi, took Motupalli from Hasan Gangu of the Bahmani Sultanate.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy kingdom?
x: Racha Vema Reddy was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy line.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kumaragiri Reddi and Rajahmundry:
1. Kumaragiri first made Rajahmundry a separate division under Anavota.
2. Kataya Vema was placed in charge of the Rajahmundry division in 1395.
3. After Pedakomati Vema seized Kondavidu, Kumaragiri died in refuge at Kondavidu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rajahmundry was first under Anavota and then Kataya Vema (1395); after Pedakomati seized Kondavidu in 1402, Kumaragiri died in refuge at Rajahmundry, not Kondavidu.

s: Which of the following statements about the political career of Kataya Vema Reddi is correct?
o: He built the Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam in 1346.
He seized Kondavidu in 1402 and caused Kumaragiri’s death.
He conquered the eastern region up to Cuttack and later administered Rajahmundry.
He abolished the tax on gold and issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli.
x: Kataya Vema, Kumaragiri’s brother-in-law and commander, conquered the eastern region up to Cuttack and later took charge of the Rajahmundry division. The other statements refer to Anavota or Pedakomati Vema, or to Prolaya Vema.

s: Of which place was Pedakomati Vema, who opposed Kumaragiri's accession, made the feudatory?
x: Kumaragiri made Pedakomati Vema the feudatory of Chandolu and designated him heir.

s: From whom did Pedakomati Vema recover lost territory in 1404?
x: Pedakomati Vema recovered lost land from Vijayanagara in 1404.

s: In which year did Prolaya Vema Reddy found the Reddy kingdom?
x: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324.

s: Prolaya Vema Reddi expelled which forces from coastal Andhra?
x: The founder Prolaya Vema Reddi expelled Tughluq forces from coastal Andhra c. 1325.

s: Which source records that Racha Vema Reddi was killed as a tyrant?
x: The Kondaveeti Kaifiyat records that Racha Vema, who levied Puriti Pannu, was killed as a tyrant.

s: Whom did Mallareddi, brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi, defeat to take Motupalli?
x: Mallareddi (Mallaya Reddy) took Motupalli by defeating Hasan Gangu, the Bahmani founder.

s: With which event in Reddi history is the Manyapuram inscription associated?
o: The restoration of Veerabhadra Reddi in 1429
The establishment of Addanki as the first capital by Prolaya Vema Reddi
The shifting of the capital from Addanki to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi
The creation of the Rajahmundry division by Kumaragiri Reddi
x: The Manyapuram inscription records the shifting of the capital to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi.

s: Who occupied the Reddi throne after Anavema Reddy?
x: In the Kondaveedu line Prolaya Vema was followed by Anavema, and Anavema by Kumaragiri Reddy.

s: With whose help did Anavema Reddi defeat the Kalinga Gajapatis?
x: Anavema Reddi defeated the Kalinga Gajapatis with assistance from the Padmanayakas and Vijayanagara.

s: Which Reddi ruler abolished the tax on gold?
x: Anavota abolished the gold tax; his minister Somaya issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli to encourage trade.

s: The 'Andhra Path', an earlier trade route, is mentioned in which Buddhist text?
x: The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra Path' (APPSC 2019). Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa and Divyavadana are other Buddhist texts not linked to the Andhra Path.

s: Which community was primarily associated with inland and coastal trade during the Reddi period?
x: The Komatis were mainly engaged in inland and coastal trade.

s: What did the Motupalli epigraph chiefly fix?
x: The Motupalli epigraph fixes commodity tariffs and shows imports and exports; famine relief belongs to the Mahasthan inscription.

s:
Assertion (A): Haravilasam is a literary work of the Reddy period that provides information on sea-borne trade.
Reason (R): Haravilasam was dedicated by Srinatha to Tippayya Setti.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Haravilasam gives information on sea-borne trade through its content, while Srinatha's dedication to the merchant Tippayya Setti is a separate fact.

s: Of which ruler was Somaya, who issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam, the minister?
x: Somaya, minister of Anavota, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam; Anavota also developed the Motupalli dock.

s: Which Reddi ruler developed the dock of the Motupalli port?
x: Motupalli was taken by Mallaya Reddy and its dock was developed by Anavota Reddi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Srinatha's Haravilasamu?
o: It was dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti
It is chiefly a source on the military organisation of the Vijayanagara Empire
It describes Reddi-period sea trade, including imports and exports
x: Haravilasamu, dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, is valued as a source on Reddi-period sea trade, imports and exports, not on Vijayanagara military organisation.

s: Who built the Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam?
x: Anavema Reddi built the Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam and the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam.

s: Which of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Patala Ganga steps — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
x: The Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam were associated with Prolaya Vema Reddi, not Pedakomati Vema Reddi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which religious combination is correctly associated with the Reddi period?
x: The Reddi kings followed Pashupata Shaivism, while the people largely followed Veerashaivism.

s: From which place did the Ghoderayas, whose disciples included the Reddi kings, propagate Shaivism?
x: The Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam; the Vadagalai matha was at Ahobilam.

s: Which of the following pairs of rulers were patrons of Vaishnavism?
x: Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema were patrons of Vaishnavism. The Reddis gradually moved from Shaivism towards Vaishnavism in the later period.

s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and the rebuilding of the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi?
x: Prolaya Vema Reddi built the pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and rebuilt the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi.

s: Prolaya Vema Reddy built stepped pathways to Ahobilam and to the Pathala Ganga descent at which place?
x: He built the Sopanamargas to ease pilgrimage to Ahobilam and the steep descent to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam.

s: Where was the Vadagalai matha patronised by Reddi Vaishnavas?
x: Vaishnavism under the Reddis centred on the Vadagalai matha at Ahobilam; Tripurantakam was the Ghoderaya Shaiva centre.

s: Which architectural work at Srisailam is attributed to Anavema Reddi?
x: Anavema Reddi built the Veerashiro Mantapa at Srisailam. The Anavemagiri mandapas were built by him at Simhachalam, while the steps to Ahobilam are associated with Prolaya Vema.

s: Who restored the Amareswara temple at Amaravati in the Reddi period?
x: Vallaya Vemana, minister of Anavota Reddi, restored the Amareswara temple at Amaravati.

s: Which title did Prolaya Vema Reddi take for his land gifts to Brahmanas?
x: Prolaya Vema's land gifts to Brahmanas earned him the title Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama.

s: Who held the title 'Dharma Durgavibhala'?
x: Dharma Durgavibhala was Prolaya Vema Reddy's title; Pedakomati Vema Reddy was known as Sarvagna.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kumaragiri Reddi was known as Karpura Vasanta Rayalu. Rajashri Ramani was a title of Anavema Reddi.

s: In which year were the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam completed, according to the Mutnuri inscription?
x: The Mutnuri inscription records the steps being finished in 1346; Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled till 1353.

s: Who held the title 'Dweepa Vijetha'?
x: Dweepa Vijetha was Anavota Reddi's title; Prolaya Vema was Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu.

s: Which title was associated with Srinatha?
x: Srinatha, the Reddy-period poet, was known as Kavisarvabhauma. Abhinava Dandi was Ketana's title, Sarvagna Pedakomati Vema Reddy's and Rayagaja Kesari Rudramadevi's.

s: Who first bore the title 'Andhra Suratrana'?
x: Andhra Suratrana was first borne by the Musunuri leader Kapaya Nayaka and was later also given to Anavema Reddi.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pedakomati Vema Reddy – Karpura Vasanta Rayalu
x: Prasadaditya (Recherla chief) was called Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya. Kumaragiri was Karpura Vasantaraya and Pedakomati Vema was Sarvajna Chakravarti (Sarvagna); Konda Venkatappaiah was Desha Bhakta.

s: Who held the title 'Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava'?
x: Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava, like Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu, was a title of Prolaya Vema Reddi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Kondavidu Reddi ruler?
o: Anavota Reddi – abolished the gold tax
Anavema Reddi – most charitable Reddi king
x: Puriti Pannu was levied by Racha Vema, not Kumaragiri; the other three pairs are correct.

s: What was the crop share given to village Ayagars as remuneration called?
x: Ayagars were paid in Manyam land or through a crop share called Mera.

s: In Kakatiya usage, on what was Pullari a tax?
x: Pullari was the cattle-grazing tax; Illari was the house tax, Ari the land tax and Kanika the gifts.

s: The village administrative system of the Reddis included how many Ayagars?
x: A Reddi village had twelve Ayagars, or village servants.

s: Which of the following pairs of Reddi village functionaries is correctly matched?
x: The Karnam was the accountant, the Reddi or Peddakapu the headman and the Talari the watchman.

s: On what was Illari, levied in the Reddi kingdom, a tax?
x: Illari was a house tax; Pullari was on grazing, Puriti Pannu on childbirth and Ari on land.

s: What did Kanika in Reddi taxation refer to?
o: Presents or gifts to the king or officials
x: Kanika meant presents or gifts to the king or officials; the crop share for Ayagars was Mera.

s: On what was the Puriti Pannu, levied by Racha Vema, a tax?
x: Puriti Pannu was a tax on childbirth levied by Racha Vema, the last Kondavidu Reddi ruler.

s: In the Reddi tax system, what was 'Ari'?
x: Ari was the land tax; Illari was the house tax, Pullari the grazing tax and Puriti Pannu the childbirth tax.

s: Whom did Kumaragiri Reddy succeed?
x: Kumaragiri Reddy succeeded Anavema Reddy; among the Kakatiyas, Rudra Deva came after Prola Raju II and Mahadeva succeeded Rudra Deva.

s: Which Rajamahendravaram figure was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414 by Gajaraju Tippa?
x: Kataya Vema was killed at Kakaraparthi (1414) by Gajaraju Tippa; Allada Reddi then ran the state as regent.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of Vijayanagara in Allada Reddi's conflict?
o: Deva Raya I supported Kataya Vema against the Kondavidu forces.
Mallappa Odayar founded the Rajahmundry branch of the Reddis.
Kapileswara Gajapati allied with Allada Reddi against Kondavidu.
Deva Raya II supported Annadeva in capturing Vengi.
x: Deva Raya I of Vijayanagara backed Kataya Vema, making Vijayanagara an ally of Allada Reddi's side.

s: With whose support did Annadeva capture parts of Vengi from Allada Reddi?
x: Annadeva captured parts of Vengi with Velama support, one of the challenges faced by Allada Reddi.

s: What was the immediate political consequence of the fall of Kondavidu in 1424?
o: Rajahmundry became a Gajapati province immediately.
Kondavidu became independent of both Vijayanagara and the Gajapati kingdom.
Rajahmundry survived for another 24 years as a Vijayanagara feudatory.
The Reddi rule over Rajahmundry ended in 1402.
x: Although Kondavidu fell in 1424, Rajahmundry continued for another 24 years as a feudatory of Vijayanagara.

s: Who expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as feudatories?
x: Deva Raya II expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as Vijayanagara feudatories.

s: In which year did Gajapati Ganga Ganapati take Rajahmundry?
x: Ganga Ganapati took Rajahmundry in 1420; Veerabhadra and Vema recovered it in 1423, Veerabhanu Deva occupied it in 1429 and Kapileswara annexed it in 1446–48.

s: Which Gajapati ruler annexed Rajahmundry during 1446–48?
x: After the death of Deva Raya II, Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48).

s: During whose reign did Kondavidu pass to Vijayanagara in 1424?
x: After the death of Racha Vema Reddi, Kondavidu passed to Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II in 1424.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the end of the Rajahmundry branch of Reddi rule?
o: It was absorbed into Kondavidu after the fall of Racha Vema.
It was conquered by Deva Raya I in 1402.
It was annexed by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.
It ended with the death of Kataya Vema in 1424.
x: The Rajahmundry branch, ruled at the end by Veerabhadra Reddi and Vema Reddi, was ended by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.

s: The Kaluvacheru inscription was issued by Anithalli, the wife of which ruler?
x: Anithalli, wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, issued the Kaluvacheru inscription.

s: Who was the prime minister and de facto ruler of the Rajahmundry Reddi kingdom from 1423 to 1448?
x: Vema (Veda) Reddi, brother of the nominal king Veerabhadra Reddi, was prime minister and de facto ruler from 1423 to 1448.

s: For whom did Allada Reddi run the Rajahmundry state as regent?
x: Allada Reddi was regent (1414–c. 1420) for Veerabhadra Reddi.

s:
Consider the following statements about Queen Anitalli:
1. She was the daughter of Kataya Vema.
2. She was the wife of Pedakomati Vema.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Anitalli was Kataya Vema's daughter and the wife of Veerabhadra Reddi; Pedakomati Vema's queen was Surambika.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler bore the title 'Gajabetekara' (hunter of elephants)?
x: Deva Raya II, the greatest Sangama ruler, bore the title Gajabetekara.

s: According to Ferishta, which kind of Muslim soldiers did Deva Raya II especially enlist in his army?
x: Ferishta says Deva Raya II hired Muslim soldiers, especially archers, to strengthen his army.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler reduced the Kandukur branch of the Reddis to feudatories?
x: Deva Raya I reduced the Kandukur Reddis (Mallareddi's line) to Vijayanagara feudatories.

s: In which year did Gajarao Tippa defeat Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta?
x: Gajarao Tippa defeated Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta in 1396; the Bahmani attack on Kandukur was repelled in 1398.

s: The Sarpavaram inscription records the marriage of Kataya Vema's son to Vijayalakshmi. Whose daughter was she?
x: The Sarpavaram inscription refers to a treaty in which Harihara II gave his daughter Vijayalakshmi in marriage to Kataya Vema's son.

s: From which region did the Reddis expel the Velamas in the Battle of Bhimavaram?
x: In the Battle of Bhimavaram (APPSC G2 2019 key) the Reddis expelled the Velamas from Palnadu.

s: Kataya Vema Reddi defeated which Vijayanagara ruler?
x: Kataya Vema beat Harihara II and took Tripurantakam and Vinukonda; the Sarpavaram treaty followed.

s: The Kaluvacheru inscription of 1423 was issued after which event?
o: The seizure of Kondavidu by Pedakomati Vema
The construction of Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam
The abolition of the gold tax by Anavota
x: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription in 1423 after the recapture of Rajahmundry. It also provides information on the Musunuri-led liberation and Prolaya Vema Reddi’s service under the Nayakas.

s: What did Muhammad bin Tughlaq rename Warangal as after its fall?
x: Warangal was renamed Sultanpurti and Andhra placed under Malik Burhanuddin, assisted by Malik Maqbul.

s: Under which Kakatiya ruler had Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi served as generals?
x: These three were the surviving generals of Prataparudra after the fall of Warangal.

s: What was the Vimochanodyamam?
o: A religious movement founded by the Velamas
The first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra
A military expedition of the Cholas into Telangana
A revenue settlement introduced by the Reddis
x: Vimochanodyamam was the first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra and was associated with the Musunuris.

s: To which period is the Recherla Velama kingdom generally dated?
x: The Recherla kingdom is dated c. 1325–1475, about 150 years; it began as loyal feudatories of the early Kakatiyas.

s: To which period is the Reddi successor state approximately dated?
x: The Reddi state is dated 1325–1448, while the Recherla Velama state is dated 1325–1475.

s: Which were the successor states that arose after the loss of Kakatiya unity?
o: Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi states
Kalyani Chalukya, Velama and Reddi states
x: The loss of Kakatiya unity gave rise to the Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi successor states.

s: The Kaluvacheru grant names how many Nayakas who backed Prolaya Nayaka?
x: The Kaluvacheru grant (1423) names 75 Nayakas who supported Prolaya Nayaka.

s: Which Reddi queen issued the Kaluvacheru grant of 1423?
x: The Kaluvacheru grant (1423) was issued by Reddi queen Anitalli; the Vilasa grant was Prolaya Nayaka's.

s: Which of the following chiefs took part in the liberation movement but did NOT lead it?
x: Koppula Prolaya Nayaka was one of the chiefs who took part; the confederacy was led by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.

s: Who was the deputy of Malik Burhanuddin in Andhra after the fall of Warangal in 1323?
x: Andhra was placed under Malik Burhanuddin with Malik Maqbul as deputy.

s: Of Prataparudra's generals, how many survived the fall of Warangal?
x: Of Prataparudra's 75 generals only three survived: Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Vilasa grant (1330) is Prolaya Nayaka's; the Kaluvacheru grant (1423) is Anitalli's.

s: The Musunuri Nayaks belonged primarily to which community?
x: The Musunuris belonged to the Kamma community, also described as Chaturthanvayas.

s: Which capital–ruler combination is correctly matched?
o: Devarakonda—Prolaya Nayaka during the liberation movement
x: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from Rekapalli. Kapaya ruled from Warangal or Orugallu from 1336, while Rachakonda and Devarakonda were associated with the Recherla Velamas.

s: Whose son was Prolaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family?
x: Prolaya Nayaka was the son of Potinayaka; being childless he was succeeded by his cousin Kapaya.

s: Who succeeded Prolaya Nayaka, who was childless?
x: Prolaya Nayaka was childless and was succeeded by his cousin Kapaya Nayaka.

s: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from which place?
x: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from Rekapalli, situated on the Godavari in the forest region near Bhadrachalam.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330):
1. It was issued by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
2. It records the restoration of agraharas to Brahmins.
3. It was issued by the Reddi queen Anitalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Prolaya Nayaka issued the Vilasa grant, which records Tughluq atrocities and the restoration of agraharas; Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru grant.

s: Which of the following is recorded in the Vilasa grant of Prolaya Nayaka?
o: Kapaya Nayaka's truce with the Bahmanis
Tughluq atrocities and the rise of Prolaya Nayaka
x: The Vilasa grant (1330) describes Tughluq atrocities, Prolaya Nayaka's rise and agrarian relief.

s: Rekapalli, the capital of Prolaya Nayaka, lay on which river near Bhadrachalam?
x: Rekapalli was on the Godavari, in the forest near Bhadrachalam.

s: Who led the confederacy of the post-Kakatiya liberation movement?
x: Prolaya Nayaka led the post-Kakatiya liberation confederacy.

s: Which work was composed by Sarvagna Singa Bhupala of Rachakonda?
x: Sarvagna Singa Bhupala, a Sanskrit scholar-king, composed Rasarnava Sudhakara, a work on dramaturgy.

s: Which of the following work–subject pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sangeeta Sudhakaram — Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
Rasarnava Sudhakaram — commentary on Sangita Ratnakara
Rasarnava Sudhakaram — Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
Sangeeta Chintamani — Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
x: Rasarnava Sudhakaram deals with Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics; Sangeeta Sudhakaram is a music work commenting on Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara.

s: To whom did Bammera Potana dedicate his Bhagavatam?
x: Potana refused Sarvajna Singama Nayaka II and dedicated his Bhagavatam to Lord Rama.

s: Why is Sangeeta Sudhakaram significant in the history of music?
o: A manual of Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
A commentary on Sarngadeva’s Sangita Ratnakara
A record of the Nayaka confederacy
A Persian account of the Bahmani wars
x: Sangeeta Sudhakaram is a musical work associated with Singabhupala II and serves as a commentary on Sarngadeva’s Sangita Ratnakara.

s: What does Rasarnava Sudhakara, composed by Singa Bhupala of Rachakonda, deal with?
x: Rasarnava Sudhakara is a work on Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics; Sangeeta Sudhakaram deals with music.

s: Who wrote Simhasana Dwatrimsika, the 32 throne stories of Vikramaditya in Telugu?
x: Koravi Goparaju, a poet patronised by the Recherla Velamas, wrote Simhasana Dwatrimsika.

s: Who acted together with Kapaya Nayaka in the recovery of Warangal in 1336?
o: Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama
Bukka I, Mahmud Gawan and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah
Annadevu, Kataya Vema and Pedakomati Vema Reddi
Hasan Gangu, Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Vinayaka Deva
x: In 1336, Kapaya Nayaka, Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama took Warangal from Malik Maqbul.

s: Which of the following was NOT a title associated with Kapaya Nayaka?
x: Andhradeshadhiswara, Katakachurakara and Andhra Suratrana were associated with Kapaya Nayaka. Kavirajamarga is not one of his titles.

s: Which Kakatiya ruler had earlier held the title Andhradesadhisvara, used by Kapaya Nayaka?
x: Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been used by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.

s: In 1336, which leader recovered Warangal?
x: Kapaya recovered Warangal, while Singama cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu.

s: Which inscription names 14 members of the Musunuri lineage, of whom only 3 ruled?
x: The Polavaram inscription names 14 members of the lineage, only 3 of whom ruled.

s: Where did Kapaya Nayaka's nephew Anapota Nayaka serve as governor?
x: Kapaya's nephew Anapota Nayaka was governor at Vengi.

s: Which of the following titles was borne by Kapaya Nayaka?
x: Kapaya held Andhra Suratrana, Andhradesadhisvara and Katakachurakara; Kavirajamarga is not his title.

s: Who, among the following, later bore the title 'Andhra Suratrana' after Kapaya Nayaka?
x: Kapaya was the first Andhra Suratrana; Anavema Reddi later held the title.

s: In which year and at which place did Kapaya Nayaka help Hasan Gangu found the Bahmani kingdom?
x: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu, also known as Zafar Khan, establish the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga in 1347.

s: In which year did Kapaya Nayaka recover Warangal from Malik Maqbul?
x: Warangal was recovered in 1336; the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 and Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356.

s: Which fort did Kapaya Nayaka cede to the Bahmanis under the truce of 1364–65?
x: Kapaya ceded Golconda fort with huge wealth, and Golconda became the boundary between the two powers.

s:
Assertion (A): The battle of Bhimavaram (1367–68) marked the end of Musunuri rule.
Reason (R): Musunuri Kapaya was killed in that battle fighting Anapota Nayaka.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Anapota Nayaka defeated Musunuri Kapaya at Bhimavaram in 1367–68; Kapaya's death ended Musunuri rule.

s: What does Ferishta's Persian work Tarikh-i-Ferishta call Telangana?
x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta calls Telangana 'Tilang' and describes the Bahmani-Kapaya conflicts.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler gave help to Kapaya Nayaka?
x: Kapaya received help from Bukka I of Vijayanagara and also sought help from Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

s: What was the principal consequence of Kapaya Nayaka’s decline in relation to the Reddis and Velamas?
o: The Reddis recovered coastal Andhra and the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana
The Velamas restored the Musunuri kingdom in coastal Andhra
The Reddis captured Telangana and the Velamas occupied coastal Andhra
Both groups lost their territories to the Bahmanis
x: Kapaya’s decline enabled the Reddis to take coastal Andhra, while the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana.

s: In which year did Kapaya Nayaka lose Bhuvanagiri to the Bahmanis?
x: Kapaya lost Kaulas in 1350 and Bhuvanagiri in 1356; Golconda was ceded in 1364-65.

s: Which Bahmani Sultan burnt alive Kapaya Nayaka's son Vinayaka Deva?
x: Muhammad Shah I had Kapaya's son Vinayaka Deva burnt alive in 1361/62.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Musunuri–Bahmani truce of 1364–65:
1. Kapaya ceded Golconda.
2. Kapaya paid 33 lakhs and a turquoise throne.
3. Bhuvanagiri became the boundary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Golconda, 33 lakhs, the turquoise throne and elephants and horses were given, and Golconda became the boundary; Bhuvanagiri had been lost in 1356.

s: To whom did Musunuri Telangana pass after the battle of Bhimavaram (1367–68)?
x: Anapota Nayaka killed Kapaya at Bhimavaram, ending the Musunuri line; Telangana passed to the Velamas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Kapaya Nayaka's losses to the Bahmanis?
x: Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356; in 1347 Kapaya helped Hasan Gangu found the Bahmani kingdom.

s: Who took coastal Andhra after Kapaya Nayaka's decline?
x: After Kapaya's decline, the Reddis took coastal Andhra and the Velamas took Musunuri Telangana.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Fall of Warangal
B. Issue of the Vilasa grant
C. Kapaya Nayaka’s capture of Orugallu
D. Battle of Bhimavaram
x: Warangal fell in 1323, the Vilasa grant was issued in 1330, Orugallu was captured in 1336, and the Battle of Bhimavaram occurred in 1367–68.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Vilasa grant was issued before Vijayanagara was founded
The Bahmani kingdom arose before Vijayanagara was founded
The truce ceding Golconda came in 1364–65
x: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 and the Bahmani kingdom only in 1347; the Vilasa grant (1330) came before both.

s: Madanayudu and his nephew Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom primarily to avenge the death of whom?
x: Madanayudu and Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom to avenge Singama.

s: At which place did Madanayudu and Naganayudu defeat Anavota Reddi?
x: Madanayudu and Naganayudu defeated Anavota Reddi at Dharanikota, also called Dannala Kota.

s: Who aided the Jallipalli Kshatriyas against Singama Nayaka at the battle of Jallipalli?
x: At Jallipalli, the Jallipalli Kshatriyas, aided by the Reddis, killed Singama.

s: After their victory at Dharanikota, the Velamas took which title?
x: After Dharanikota the Velamas took the titles Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga.

s: Which of the following battle–outcome pairs is correctly matched?
x: Singama died at Jallipalli; Kapaya was killed at Bhimavaram; the Velamas won at Dharanikota.

s: With whose assistance did Mahmud Gawan suppress the Telangana revolts?
x: Bahmani minister Mahmud Gawan put down the Telangana revolts with Velama assistance.

s: Against whom were the later alliances of the Velamas mainly directed?
x: The Velamas allied with the Bahmanis and Gajapatis against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler allied with the Velamas?
x: Devaraya I of Vijayanagara formed an alliance with the Velamas.

s: In which year did Pedakomati Vema Reddi die fighting the Velamas?
x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi died fighting the Velamas in 1420.

s: Lingamanidu of Devarakonda sought help from which Gajapati prince?
x: Lingamanidu of Devarakonda sought help from Gajapati Hamvira.

s: From whom did the Velamas help Annadevu take Vengi?
x: The Velamas helped Annadevu take Vengi from Kataya Vema.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Velamas' foreign relations:
1. Deva Raya I of Vijayanagara allied with them.
2. Mahmud Gawan crushed the Telangana revolts with their help.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Deva Raya I allied with the Velamas, and Mahmud Gawan used Velama help against the Telangana revolts.

s: To which place did Anapota Reddy move the Reddy capital from Addanki?
x: Prolaya Vema Reddi ruled from Addanki and Anapota Reddy moved the capital to Kondaveedu.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Pithapuram line was associated with the Pithapuram estate in the Godavari region, not Rachakonda. Damerla, Velugoti and Ravu are correctly matched with Sri Kalahasti, Venkatagiri and Bobbili respectively.

s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Musunuri Nayaks ruled from Rekapalli; the Satavahanas ruled from Paithan, the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri and the Salankayanas from Vengipuram.

s: Under the Poligar system, which landed families became zamindars?
x: Under the Poligar system, Velama, Reddi and Raju landed families became zamindars.

s: Which region did the Velugoti branch of the Velamas rule?
x: Velugoti = Venkatagiri; Ravu = Bobbili; Damerla = Sri Kalahasti.

s: Which Velama family ruled Bobbili?
x: The Ravu family ruled Bobbili.

s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Reddi capitals were Addanki, Kondaveedu and Rajahmundry; Devarakonda was a Recherla capital.

s: Which dynasty had Vengipuram as its capital?
x: The Salankayanas ruled from Vengipuram; the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri and the Satavahanas from Paithan.

s: Which of the following pairs of dynasty/janapada and capital is correctly matched?
x: The Kakatiyas first ruled from Anamakonda; Assaka's capital was Bodhan, Anupa's Mahishmathi and the Brihatpalayanas' Koduru.

s: What was the capital of Anupa under Gautamiputra Satakarni?
x: Mahishmathi was the capital of Anupa; Koduru was the Brihatpalayana capital and Penugonda the post-Tallikota Vijayanagara capital.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Paithan was the capital of the Satavahanas.
Vengipuram was the capital of the Salankayanas.
Vijayapuri was the capital of the Ikshvakus.
Anamakonda was the only capital of the Kakatiyas.
x: Anamakonda (Hanamakonda) was only the first Kakatiya capital; the capital later moved to Warangal (Orugallu).

s: Which of the following Velama family–region pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Ravu ruled Bobbili; the Pithapuram estate was a separate line.

s: Who founded the Recherla Velama lineage?
x: Betala Nayudu is identified as the founder of the Recherla lineage.

s: Which of the following statements about Singama Nayaka I is correct?
o: He founded the independent kingdom and expanded towards the Krishna and the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
He shifted the capital from Rachakonda to Amanagallu
He founded the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga
He defeated Sultan Quli Qutb Shah and recovered Devarakonda
x: Singama Nayaka I founded the independent Velama kingdom and expanded to the Krishna and into the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.

s: What did Devarakonda serve as?
o: The initial capital of Prolaya Nayaka
The capital of Kapaya Nayaka before 1323
The second branch capital of the Recherla Velamas
The capital of the Reddis before Addanki
x: Devarakonda in Nalgonda was the second branch capital of the Recherla Velamas.

s: To which place did Anapota Nayaka, the son of Singama Nayaka I, shift the capital from Amanagallu?
x: Anapota Nayaka transferred the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda.

s: Which work is the family history of the Recherla Velamas?
x: The Velugoti Varivamsavali is the family history of the Recherla Velamas. Madhura Vijayam is Gangadevi's poem, Rasarnava Sudhakara is Singabhupala's work on dramaturgy, and Tarikh-i-Ferishta is a Persian history of the Deccan sultans.

s: Which Sultan defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed both Rachakonda and Devarakonda?
o: Muhammad I of the Bahmani dynasty
x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, who ruled at Golconda from 1518 to 1543, defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

s: Who killed Singama Nayaka I, the founder of the independent Recherla kingdom?
x: Singama Nayaka I was killed by the Jallipalli chiefs, not at Bhimavaram.

s: Whose younger brother was Mada Nayaka, who was made ruler of Devarakonda?
x: Mada Nayaka, younger brother of Anavota (Anapota) Nayaka, was made ruler of Devarakonda.

s: Who succeeded Mada Nayaka as ruler of Devarakonda?
x: Mada Nayaka's son Pedda Vedagiri succeeded him at Devarakonda.

s: The Rachakonda fort is noted for which construction technique?
x: Rachakonda fort is built in cyclopean masonry without mortar.

s: What kind of fort is the Devarakonda fort of the Recherla kings?
x: Devarakonda is a 14th-century hilltop fort of the Recherla kings.

s: By what other name were the Recherla Velamas known?
x: The Recherla Velamas were also called Padmanayakas; Chaturthanvayas refers to the Kamma clan of the Musunuris.

s:
Consider the following statements about Anapota Nayaka:
1. He was the son of Singama Nayaka I.
2. He shifted the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda.
3. He moved the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Anapota Nayaka (Velama), Singama's son, moved the capital to Rachakonda; it was Anapota Reddi who moved the Reddi capital to Kondaveedu.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Betala Nayudu — Founder of the Recherla lineage
Singama Nayaka I — Killed in the Battle of Bhimavaram
Anapota Nayaka — Shifted the capital to Rachakonda
Sarvagna Singa Bhupala — Scholar-king of Rachakonda
x: Singama Nayaka I was killed fighting the chiefs of Jallipalli, whereas Anapota Nayaka defeated Kapaya at Bhimavaram.

s: Which Bahmani Sultan shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
x: Ahmad Shah I moved the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar (PYQ G2 2003). Hasan Gangu founded the kingdom with Gulbarga as its capital in 1347. Muhammad Shah I fought Kapaya Nayaka, and Muhammad III ruled with Mahmud Gawan as his minister.

s: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in which century?
x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347, in the 14th century.

s: What was Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, renamed?
x: The first Bahmani capital Gulbarga was named Hasanabad.

s: In which year was Mahmud Gawan, under whom the Bahmani kingdom was largest, executed?
x: Mahmud Gawan, minister of Muhammad III, was executed in 1481, which broke the kingdom apart.

s: By what other name was Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder of the Bahmani kingdom, known?
x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, also called Hasan Gangu or Zafar Khan, founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four regions of the early Bahmani kingdom?
x: The early Bahmani kingdom had four regions: Gulbarga, Daulatabad, Berar and Bidar; Golconda was not one of them.

s: With the capture of which place did Krishnadevaraya's campaign against Prataparudra Gajapati begin?
x: The campaign went through Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Bejawada, then the march to Cuttack in 1518.

s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the terms of peace between Krishnadevaraya and Prataparudra Gajapati?
o: Annexation of Cuttack and the Gajapati heartland to Vijayanagara
Marriage of Prataparudra's daughter to Krishnadevaraya
Return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati
x: The peace terms were the marriage of Prataparudra's daughter to Krishnadevaraya, the gift of the Balakrishna idol and the return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati, who stayed as a feudatory. Cuttack and the Gajapati heartland were NOT taken over.

s: Who drove the Gajapatis out of south-eastern Andhra by about 1470 and subsequently occupied territory up to the Godavari?
x: Saluva Narasimha drove the Gajapatis out of south-eastern Andhra by about 1470 and extended his occupation up to the Godavari.

s: How long did the siege of Udayagiri last before it fell to Krishnadevaraya?
x: Udayagiri fell first, after an 18-month siege.

s: Which daughter of Prataparudra Gajapati did Krishnadevaraya marry?
x: Prataparudra's daughter Annapurna Devi (also Bhadradevi/Tukkadevi/Jaganmohini) married Krishnadevaraya.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishnadevaraya–Prataparudra peace:
1. Lands north of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati.
2. Cuttack was annexed to Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Lands north of the Krishna were returned and the Gajapati stayed a feudatory; Cuttack was not taken over.

s: Where do Krishnadevaraya's victory pillars over the Gajapatis stand?
x: The victory pillars at Simhachalam and Potnuru mark Krishnadevaraya's triumph over the Gajapatis.

s: Whose son was Hamvira, who defeated the Bahmani army attacking Devarakonda?
x: Hamvira was the son of Kapileswara Gajapati and defeated the Bahmani army that attacked Devarakonda.

s: During which period did the Gajapatis rule?
x: The Gajapati rule is dated approximately from 1434 to 1541.

s: Among the Gajapati rulers, whose Andhra campaigns came first?
x: Kapilendra, the founder, campaigned first; Purushottama followed and Prataparudra came after him.

s: Which of the following correctly describes Kapilendra Gajapati's Andhra campaigns?
o: He defeated Saluva Narasimha and occupied Cuttack.
He founded the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga and annexed Bidar.
He recovered Udayagiri from Krishnadevaraya and restored Gajapati control over Kondapalli.
He attacked Tiran Andhra in 1448 and captured Kondaveedu around 1450.
x: Kapilendra attacked Tiran Andhra in 1448 and captured Kondaveedu around 1450. The other alternatives attribute later or unrelated events to him.

s: To whom did Prataparudra Gajapati lose Udayagiri, Kondaveedu and Kondapalli?
x: Prataparudra Gajapati lost these forts to Krishnadevaraya (1513–1519).

s: What does the title 'Gajapati' mean?
x: Gajapati means 'Lord of Elephants'; the Gajapatis ruled from Cuttack.

s: Which Gajapati ruler refused to help the Bahmani Sultan Muhammad III?
x: Purushottama refused to help Muhammad III and recovered ground from the Bahmanis.

s: In 1471 the Bahmanis installed which Gajapati prince as their puppet?
x: Hamvira was installed as a Bahmani puppet in 1471 and was overturned by Purushottama.

s: Which was the capital of the Gajapatis?
x: Gajapati means Lord of Elephants; their capital was Cuttack.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kapilendra Gajapati:
1. He founded the Gajapati line.
2. He took Kondaveedu around 1450.
3. He lost Udayagiri to Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kapilendra founded the line and took Kondaveedu c. 1450; Udayagiri was lost by Prataparudra.

s: Around which year did Kondaveedu, held by Vijayanagara until 1449, fall to the Gajapatis?
x: Kondaveedu was under Vijayanagara until 1449 and fell to the Gajapatis around 1450.

s: After which year did Gajapati Kapileswara take Rajamahendravaram from the Reddis?
x: Kapileswara took Rajamahendravaram after 1446, after Deva Raya II's death, ending the Rajahmundry Reddis.

s: Which Vijayanagara commander helped the Reddis of Rajamahendravaram, as recorded in the Draksharama inscription (1444)?
x: The Draksharama inscription (1444) records help from Vijayanagara commander Mallappa Odayar.

s: Udayagiri, a major Gajapati stronghold in southern Andhra, is in which present district?
x: Udayagiri (Nellore) was the major Gajapati stronghold in southern Andhra.

s: What were the revenue officers in the southern Andhra territories of the Gajapati Empire known as?
x: Naidu was the title used for revenue officers in the southern Andhra regions of the Gajapati Empire.

s: Which local chiefs collected revenue and maintained order under Gajapati rule in Andhra?
x: Nayakas and samantas collected revenue and maintained order; the Reddi-era social order was retained.

s: What was a Dandapata under Gajapati administration?
o: Large province with a standing army
x: Dandapata was a large province (whole districts) with a standing army.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gajapati administration in Andhra?
o: Naidu was a revenue officer in southern Andhra
A Dandapata was a large province with a standing army
The Reddi-era social order was abolished
x: The Reddi-era social order was kept under the Gajapatis.

s: Who repulsed Firoz Shah's army at Kandukuru in 1398?
x: Machareddi repulsed Firoz Shah at Kandukuru in 1398; Gajarao Tippa beat him at Kambhammetta in 1396.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Shah I — Burning Vinayaka alive in 1361
Mahmud Gawan — Moving the capital to Bidar
x: Muhammad Shah I burned Kapaya's son Vinayaka alive in 1361. Orugallu was subdued by Muhammad III and Mahmud Gawan (not Firoz Shah), Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar, and Mahmud Gawan was executed in 1481.

s: Which Bahmani leader subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu?
x: With Muhammad III, Mahmud Gawan suppressed Telangana revolts from 1453, subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu.

s: Who beat Firoz Shah's Bahmani army at Kambhammetta in 1396?
x: Kambhammetta (1396) = Gajarao Tippa; Kandukuru (1398) = Machareddi.

s: Firoz Shah allied with Pedakomati against which place in 1417?
x: Firoz Shah allied with Pedakomati against Rajamahendravaram in 1417.

s: In which year did Muhammad III and Mahmud Gawan push into Odisha?
x: Muhammad III and Mahmud Gawan took Kondaveedu and pushed into Odisha in 1471.

s: Which of the following Bahmani incursion–opponent pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kandukuru (1398) = Machareddi; Kambhammetta (1396) = Gajarao Tippa.

s: In which source is Kapilendra's attack on Tiran Andhra in 1448 recorded?
x: The Penugonda inscription records Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra (1448).

s: Between which rivers does the Raichur Doab lie?
x: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra; Rajahmundry and Kondaveedu lie in the Krishna–Godavari region.

s: Whom did Krishnadevaraya defeat in the Battle of Raichur (1520)?
x: In the Battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya beat Bijapur.

s: Among whom was the rivalry over the Krishna–Godavari region of coastal Andhra mainly fought?
x: Coastal Andhra (Krishna–Godavari) was contested by the Gajapatis, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis; the Raichur Doab was Bahmani vs Vijayanagara.

s: What is the Madala Panji?
o: A temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri dealing with Gajapati history
A Persian history of the Deccan sultans
A military account of Kapileswara's attack on Andhra
An inscription describing Vijayanagara assistance to the Reddis
x: Madala Panji is the temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri and contains material on Gajapati history.

s: Which of the following source–information pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anantavaram inscription – Vijayanagara help to the Reddis
Penugonda inscription – Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra in 1448
Draksharama inscription – Krishnadevaraya's triumph over the Gajapatis
Victory pillars at Simhachalam and Potnuru – Defeat of the Virupaksharayas
x: The Penugonda inscription records Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra in 1448. Anantavaram records the Virupaksharayas' defeat, Draksharama Vijayanagara help to the Reddis, and the victory pillars Krishnadevaraya's triumph.

s: What were the Virupaksharayas made to pay, according to the Anantavaram inscription of Prataparudra?
x: The Anantavaram inscription says the Virupaksharayas were defeated and made to pay Kappam.

s: Which Persian history of the Deccan sultans gives the Bahmani side of their wars in Andhra?
x: Ferishta's Persian history gives the Bahmani side; Madala Panji is the Puri temple chronicle of the Gajapatis.

s: Over which three historical eras was the Telugu Mahabharata completed?
o: Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi eras
Vijayanagara, Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi eras
x: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over three successive eras: the Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi periods.

s: Who held the title 'Ubhayakavimitrudu'?
x: Ubhayakavimitrudu is Tikkana's title; Nannaya was Vaganusasana and Errana Sambhudasa.

s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana translate into Telugu?
x: Tikkana translated the remaining 15 parvas, from Virata to Swargarohana, and called it Prabandha Mandali.

s: Whose court poet was Tikkana?
x: Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II of Nellore; Errana was at Prolaya Vema Reddi's court and Rajaraja Narendra patronised Nannaya.

s: Which of the following poet–title pairs is correctly matched?
x: Nannaya is Adikavi; Tikkana is Kavibrahma and Errana is Prabandha Parameswara.

s: Errana completed which parva of the Mahabharata left unfinished by Nannaya?
x: By completing the Aranya Parva, Errana linked Nannaya's work with Tikkana's.

s: Which of the following correctly describes Nannaya's contribution to the Telugu Mahabharata?
o: The complete Virata to Swargarohana Parvas
The Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of Aranya Parva
The Adi, Sabha and the remaining part of Aranya Parva
x: Nannaya translated the Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of the Aranya Parva. Errana later completed the remaining portion of Aranya.

s: Whose court poet was Nannaya, the Adikavi whose Andhra Mahabharatamu is regarded as the first book in Telugu?
x: Nannaya was court poet, teacher and adviser of the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra (r. 1018-1061) at Rajamahendravaram. Prolaya Vema Reddi patronised Errana; Manumasiddhi II patronised Tikkana; Ganapatideva was the Kakatiya ruler of Tikkana's age.

s: Which of the following was a member of the Kavitraya?
x: The Kavitraya consists of Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.

s: To which century did Errana, the last of the Kavitrayam, belong?
x: Nannaya – 11th, Tikkana – 13th, Errana – 14th century.

s: Who held the title 'Prabandha Parameswara'?
x: Errana held the titles Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa.

s: From where did Rajaraja Narendra, Nannaya's patron, rule?
x: Rajaraja Narendra (r. 1018–1061), Eastern Chalukya, ruled from Rajamahendravaram.

s: Which parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana translate?
x: Tikkana translated the remaining 15 parvas, Virata to Swargarohana.

s: Which of the following poet–title pairs is correctly matched?
x: Errana = Sambhudasa; Nannaya = Adikavi; Tikkana = Kavibrahma; Srinatha = Kavisarvabhauma.

s: Who among the Kavitrayam was known as 'Kavibrahma'?
x: Tikkana bore the title Kavibrahma; Nannaya was Adikavi and Errana was Sambhudasa.

s: In which language did Sarala Dasa compose the Mahabharata?
x: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia; Kasirama Das composed it in Bengali.

s: In which language is Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya, a Mahabharata, written?
x: Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya (Pampa Bharata) is in Kannada.

s: In which language did Kasirama Das compose the Mahabharata?
x: Kasirama Das wrote the Bengali Mahabharata; Sarala Dasa's is Odia.

s: Which of the following composer–language pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia; Kasirama Das's is Bengali.

s: Which of the following pairs (Telugu poet – title) is correctly matched?
x: Errapragada was Prabandha Parameswara; Nannaya was Adikavi and Tikkana was Kavibrahma.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Poet)
A. Nannaya
B. Tikkana
C. Errapragada
D. Allasani Peddana
List-II (Title)
1. Kavibrahma
2. Andhra Kavita Pitamaha
3. Adikavi
4. Prabandha Parameswara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Nannaya is Adikavi, Tikkana Kavibrahma, Errapragada Prabandha Parameswara and Peddana Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

s: Which title did Narayana Bhattu, who knew eight languages, bear?
x: Narayana Bhattu was Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara and represented Someshwara I of Kalyani at Rajamahendravaram.

s: Which of the following grant–recipient pairs is correctly matched?
x: Nandampudi agrahara was associated with Narayana Bhattu, while Navakhandavada agrahara was granted to Pavuluri Mallana.

s: Who made Narayana Bhattu his representative at Rajamahendravaram?
x: Someshwara I of Kalyani made Narayana Bhattu his representative at Rajamahendravaram.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the first mathematics book in Telugu?
o: Sara Sangraha Ganitam of Pavuluri Mallana
x: Pavuluri Mallana's Sara Sangraha Ganitam (Pavuluri Ganitam), from Mahaviracharya's Ganita Sara Sangraha, is the first mathematics book and first scientific kavya in Telugu (G2 2019 key). Andhra Shabda Chintamani is grammar, Kavijanasrayam prosody and Nitisara polity.

s:
Consider the following statements about Pavuluri Mallana:
1. He wrote the first Telugu mathematics book.
2. He received the Navakhandavada agrahara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Pavuluri Mallana wrote Sara Sangraha Ganitam and received Navakhandavada from Rajaraja Narendra.

s: Which philosophy did Tikkana, who dedicated his work to Hariharanatha, preach?
x: Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita, the unity of Shiva and Vishnu; Ketana was his disciple.

s: What was Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi?
x: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam was Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi; Basava Puranam is by Palkuriki Somanatha.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Harivamsam was written by Nannaya.
2. Uttara Harivamsa was written by Nachana Somana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: Harivamsam is Errana's, dedicated to Prolaya Vema. Statement 2 is correct: Uttara Harivamsa is by Nachana Somana. So 2 only.

s: To whom did Errana dedicate his Harivamsam?
x: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to Prolaya Vema Reddi.

s: Which disciple of Tikkana wrote Markandeya Puranam in Telugu?
x: Marana, a disciple of Tikkana, wrote Markandeya Puranam; Baddena wrote Sumathi Satakam and Manchana Keyurabahu Charitra.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its literary description?
o: Ranganatha Ramayanam — first Telugu Ramayana and first dwipada kavya
x: Ranganatha Ramayanam, by Gona Budda Reddy, is described as the first Telugu Ramayana and the first dwipada kavya.

s: Of which Sanskrit work is Manchena's Keyurabahu Charitra a Telugu rendering?
x: Manchena rendered Viddhasalabhanjika as Keyurabahu Charitra in Telugu.

s: Who wrote Sumathi Satakam?
x: Baddena wrote Sumathi Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali.

s: In which form is Ranganatha Ramayanam of Gona Budda Reddy the first Telugu kavya?
x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is the first Telugu Ramayana and the first dwipada kavya.

s: Who wrote Bhaskara Ramayanam?
x: Bhaskara Ramayanam is by Hulakki Bhaskara; Ranganatha Ramayanam is by Gona Budda Reddy.

s: Who coined the epithet 'Italian of the East' for Telugu?
x: It was coined by the 15th-century Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti; 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' is Krishnadevaraya's.

s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian family?
x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian with Gondi and Kui; Tamil and Malayalam are South Dravidian.

s: Telugu, the official language of Andhra Pradesh, belongs to which language family?
x: Telugu belongs to the Dravidian family and is one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages.

s: From which three Shaiva centres does the Trilinga theory derive the name Andhra?
x: The Trilinga theory refers to Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama as the three Shaiva centres of Trilinga desa.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telugu?
o: It has been a classical language of India since 2008
Telugu Language Day falls on 29 August
Telugu Language Day marks the birth anniversary of Gurajada Apparao
29 August is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
x: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary, not Gurajada Apparao's.

s: Which languages are sisters of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch?
x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian with Gondi and Kui; Tamil and Malayalam are South Dravidian.

s: Which is the second official language of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Telugu is the official language of AP; Urdu is the second official language.

s: Niccolo de' Conti called Telugu the 'Italian of the East' because its words:
x: Conti, a 15th-century Venetian traveller, compared Telugu to Italian because its words end in vowels.

s: Whose birth anniversary is marked by Telugu Language Day, 29 August?
x: 29 August is Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary, not Gurajada's.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Italian of the East' was coined by Niccolo de' Conti.
2. 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' occurs in Amuktamalyada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Conti, a Venetian traveller, coined the epithet; Krishnadevaraya wrote the line in Amuktamalyada.

s: In which year was Telugu given the status of a classical language?
x: Telugu became a classical language in 2008 (Tamil in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Malayalam in 2013).

s: Since the 2022 amendment, in which districts of Andhra Pradesh is Urdu the second official language?
x: Since the 2022 amendment Urdu is the second official language in all districts of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Along with Telugu, which language was declared a classical language on 31 October 2008?
x: Telugu and Kannada were both declared classical languages on 31 October 2008.

s: How many Indian languages have classical language status after the decision of October 2024?
x: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added on 3 October 2024 to the earlier six, making 11.

s: Who identified the word ‘Nagabu’ in the Amaravati inscription?
x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastri identified ‘Nagabu’ as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: ‘Vepuru’ appears in the Myakadoni inscription. ‘Andhrapatha’ belongs to the Mayidavolu plates, ‘Nagabu’ to Amaravati, and ‘-ambul’ to Vishnukundin plates.

s: In which centuries did the separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs emerge?
x: After the Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant and the common Old Kannada–Telugu script, the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.

s: Which of the following describes the Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions?
o: Sanskrit inscriptions in the common Old Kannada script
Tamil inscriptions in the Grantha script
Prakrit inscriptions in a variant of Brahmi carrying early Telugu place and personal names
Telugu inscriptions in the fully developed medieval Telugu script
x: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, dated approximately to 400 BCE in Guntur, use a variant of Brahmi and contain early Telugu place and personal names.

s: What was the royal language in the Prakrit age of Andhra, whose golden age came under Hala?
x: Prakrit was the royal language in this age (APPSC G2 2011 key), with its golden age under Hala. Sanskrit later became the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas; Telugu appears only as words in Prakrit records; Tamil is not the answer.

s: The Telugu word 'Vepuru' occurs in which inscription?
x: 'Vepuru' is from the Myakadoni inscription; 'Nagabu' from Amaravati.

s: Which dynasty issued the Chikkulla plates, in which the Telugu plural form '-ambul' appears?
x: The Chikkulla plates of the Vishnukundins use the plural '-ambul' (Vijayarajya Samvatsarambul).

s: In which script was Telugu written in the early medieval (Kadamba–Chalukya) period?
x: In the Kadamba–Chalukya period a common Old Kannada–Telugu script was used; the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.

s: Which is regarded as the first Telugu word found in an inscription?
x: 'Nagabu' in the Amaravati inscription is the first Telugu word, identified by Veturi Prabhakara Sastri.

s: Telugu words such as atta, potta, pilla and pandi are found in which Prakrit work?
x: Hala's Prakrit Gatha Saptasati contains Telugu words like atta, addam, potta, tuppu, pilla and pandi.

s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, belongs to which dynasty?
x: The Kalamalla inscription of about 575 CE is associated with the Renati Chola ruler Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya.

s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and is written in a song or geya style?
x: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara of the Renati Cholas is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and uses a song or geya style.

s: Which inscription contains the first Madhyakkara poem?
x: Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara poem; Addanki is the first Telugu poetic inscription in Taruvoja metre.

s: Who issued the Addanki inscription, the first Telugu poetic inscription?
o: Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III
x: The Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre was issued by Panduranga (Pandaranga), commander of the Eastern Chalukya king Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Yuddhamalla II issued the Bezawada inscription, Punyakumara the Erragudipadu inscription and Kubja Vishnuvardhana the Chejarla inscription.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I — first complete early Telugu prose inscription
Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana — more than 50 per cent Telugu words
Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I — first complete early Telugu text
Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first Telugu poetic inscription
x: Pitikayagulla is associated with the eighth century and post-Badami Chalukya influence, particularly in relation to early Telugu script; it is not the first Telugu poetic inscription. That distinction belongs to Addanki.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya?
x: Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada show pre-Nannaya written Telugu; the Motupalli epigraph is a later Kakatiya-era record.

s: Why is the Chebrolu inscription significant?
o: The transition from Sanskrit to Tamil exclusively
The first use of the Madhyakkara metre
x: The Chebrolu inscription is noted for showing the Marga and Desi forms.

s: Who issued the Vipparla inscription?
x: Vipparla is Jayasimha Vallabha I's (G2 2017 key); Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's.

s: To whose reign does the Chejarla inscription, with over 50% Telugu words, belong?
x: Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's inscription with over 50% Telugu words.

s: To about which year is the Kalamalla inscription, the first Telugu inscription, dated?
x: Kalamalla (Kadapa), by Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, dates to c. 575 CE.

s: The first poetic inscription in Telugu, at Addanki, is in which metre?
x: Addanki is the first poetic inscription, in Taruvoja; Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara.

s: Who issued the Bezawada inscription with the first Madhyakkara poem?
x: The Bezawada (Nagamalleswara temple) inscription is Yuddhamalla II's.

s: Which metre is used in the Kandukur inscription of Gunaga Vijayaditya?
x: Kandukur and Dharmavaram use Seesa and Ataveladi.

s: In which language were the grant details written in bilingual Eastern Chalukya records?
x: Eastern Chalukya records gave the praise in Sanskrit and the grant details in Telugu.

s: Which of the following inscription–metre pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Addanki is in Taruvoja; the first Madhyakkara is in the Bezawada inscription.

s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic and literary situation during the Kakatiya period?
o: Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed, and Telugu became the main language of inscriptions.
Persian became the principal language of Kakatiya inscriptions.
Only Tamil was used for literary composition and inscriptions.
Telugu literature declined, while Sanskrit disappeared from inscriptions.
x: In the Kakatiya era most inscriptions were in Telugu, which grew as an administrative language, and Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed. Persian and Tamil were not the Kakatiya inscriptional languages, and Telugu literature flourished rather than declined.

s: Which was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas?
x:
Most books and keys: Telugu. Strictly: the prasasti and much of the court record were in Sanskrit.
APPSC keys and NextGen give Telugu as the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas (G2 2008); Sanskrit stayed the language of the grants' prasasti.

s: Which Renati Chola ruler issued the Erragudipadu inscription?
x: The Erragudipadu inscription, the first fully available Telugu inscription, is of Punyakumara.

s: In June 2026, an ASI survey copied 25 inscriptions of the 2nd to 16th centuries in which tiger reserve?
x: In June 2026 an ASI survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve copied 25 inscriptions (2nd–16th centuries).

s: With whom is the line 'Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa' associated?
x: The line is associated with Krishnadevaraya, whose period with the Ashtadiggajas was the peak of Telugu literary culture.

s: Which Kakatiya ruler built the Kesari Samudra tank?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Prola I); it is added as option 5.
The Kesari (Arikesari) Samudram tank at Kesamudram was built by Prola I (APPSC G2 2019), not Rudradeva, Ganapatideva, Prola II or Prataparudra.

s: Who wrote Premabhiramam, the Sanskrit play of which Kreedabhiramam is a Telugu rendering?
x: Kreedabhiramam renders Ravipati Tripurantakudu's Premabhiramam, hence the authorship debate with Vinukonda Vallabharaya.

s: Who wrote Nritta Ratnavali?
x: Jayapa Senani wrote Nritta Ratnavali along with Geeta and Vadya Ratnavali; Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam.

s:
Assertion (A): Jayapa Senani authored Nrittaratnavali.
Reason (R): Jayapa Senani's profession was Gaja Sahini.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Jayapa Senani was Gaja Sahini (elephant commander) under Ganapatideva, and his military post does not explain his writing the dance treatise Nrittaratnavali.
